title: Incident investigation playbook — span summaries, shortcuts, and priority filters
content:
Purpose:
- Create a lightweight, repeatable playbook for engineers and SREs to investigate high-latency or error-heavy traces in the Console. Focus: fast situational triage with minimal clicks and clear next steps.

Context / problem statements (collected from support/incidents):
- On-call wants to find the root span quickly without stepping through dozens of spans manually.
- Team members often open the trace, see a dense waterfall, and aren't sure which spans are the real suspects (model infer, network hop, proxy, retry).
- Current filters are powerful but buried; building an ad-hoc filter during an incident is slow.
- Repeated investigations show a small set of heuristics (e.g., spans with >90th pct latency, error codes, repeated retries) are sufficient to prioritize.

Goals for this doc:
1) Define a minimal set of UI primitives (span summary chips, incident mode toggle, priority filter builder, quick actions) that let an engineer get from open-trace -> probable root in < 45s.
2) Provide wireframe-lean descriptions and interaction notes for design/engineering to prototype.
3) Produce grooming tasks with acceptance criteria for a 2-sprint rollout.

Key UX primitives (candidate list):
- Incident Mode toggle (top-left): expands filter shortcuts and highlights priority spans. When ON: timeline compresses non-priority spans, timeline shows an incident heatline.
- Span Summary Chips: small badges inline with span rows that surface 3 signals: latency (p90/p95), error marker, retry-count. Hover shows quick stats (avg, max, sample stack). Click expands detail pane.
- Priority Filter Builder (one-line query bar): pre-seeded tokens: latency:>500ms, status:>=500, retries:>0, model:~(gpt-4/open-weights), host:!=cache. Users can combine with AND/OR and save as "investigation presets".
- Jump-to-Parent / Jump-to-Children quick actions: arrow buttons on each span to navigate tree without collapsing/expanding the whole view. Useful when depth is large.
- Collapse-by-similarity: group contiguous spans with same name/resource (e.g., repeated cache-miss entries) into a collapsed stack with a count and aggregated timing.
- Compact Waterfall mode: reduces vertical span height and shows a micro-timeline overview to maintain context for long traces.
- Annotated Timeline Heatline: overlaid bar showing where 95th/99th lat spikes occur across the trace; clicking a hotspot filters to spans overlapping that time window.

Wireframe / layout notes (left-to-right):
Left column (narrow): trace metadata + incident actions\  - Trace ID / timestamp / region\  - Incident Mode toggle and preset menu\  - Save as bookmark / copy trace link\Middle column (main): waterfall + span rows\  - Compact waterfall header with timeline ruler and heatline\  - Each row: span row label, service badge, duration bar, span summary chips, quick actions (jump, focus, pin)
  - Collapsible grouping rows with aggregated timing and expand control\Right column (panel): span inspector
  - First tab: quick summary (name, full duration, parent/child counts, top 3 logs)\  - Second tab: raw data/headers and sample payload (truncated)\  - Third tab: related resources (hosts, model version, route config)

Interaction details / micro-flows:
- Open trace -> Incident Mode auto-suggestion: If trace has >2 spans with errors or 95th latency > threshold (configurable), show a subtle CTA: "Enable incident view".
- Clicking a heatline hotspot: timeline zooms to +/- 250ms of the hotspot and highlights overlapping spans. This action also pre-applies a filter: spans.overlap(timeWindow).
- Span chip click vs span row click: chip toggles selection (multi-select allowed). row click sets inspector focus and scrolls timeline to center that span.
- Keyboard shortcuts: 
  - I = toggle Incident Mode\  - F = open filter bar\  - J/K = jump prev/next priority span (skipping collapsed groups)\  - Enter = open inspector
- Multi-select behavior: shift+click selects contiguous spans; ctrl/cmd+click selects arbitrary spans. Once multiple selected, CLI-like actions appear: group, compare, export as JSON.

Design tradeoffs and rationale:
- Aggressive grouping vs fidelity: collapsing similar spans reduces noise but may obscure causality. Default collapsed when >5 repeats, with easy expand.
- Incident Mode as thin layer vs separate view: preference for an overlay mode rather than different route so bookmarks/links remain valid.
- Heatline sampling resolution: prefer 50ms buckets for interactive speed; allow higher-res in inspector.

Backlog / grooming items (ordered by priority):
1) INF-1423: Implement incident-mode toggle + basic preset filters (latency, errors, retries). Acceptance: toggle highlights priority spans and applies preset filter; unit tests for preset parsing. (2 dev wks)
2) UX-354: Span summary chips — UI and hover tooltip. Acceptance: chips render for each span and show hover card with top-3 metrics. (1.5 dev wks)
3) GH-2876: Heatline + hotspot click -> time-window filter. Acceptance: click zooms + filters as described and history state saved. (2 dev wks)
4) INF-1430: Keyboard shortcuts for incident actions; onboarding hint. Acceptance: shortcuts functional in Console and documentable in help. (1 dev wk)
5) INF-1431: Collapse-by-similarity server-side aggregation endpoint. Acceptance: endpoint returns aggregated buckets with counts and aggregated timings; UI consumes it to render collapsed rows. (3 dev wks)

Acceptance criteria (overall):
- Average time-to-first-suspect measured in lab tests is <45s for a 200-span trace with injected latency spikes.
- Incident-mode default presets detect 80% of known incident traces (historical test corpus).
- No data-loss in collapsed mode — users must be able to expand every grouping to the raw spans.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should incident presets be shareable across orgs or per-user? (ops vs personal preferences)
- Where to store saved presets (Console backend: user prefs vs org config)?
- How to model cost/permissions for exporting spans? (sensitive payloads)
- Do we allow custom time-window sizes for hotspot zooms or have fixed buckets?

Next steps / owners:
- Aisha: run sampling experiment on 1000 historical traces to validate preset thresholds (due 2025-01-20).
- Marcus: prototype span chips + hover card in Figma and add microcopy for hover states (due 2025-01-22).
- Drew: spike for server-side aggregation endpoint and API shape (due 2025-01-30).
- Elena: write acceptance tests and coordinate UX engineering grooming (due 2025-02-03).

Notes / snippets collected from Slack and incidents: 
- "If the model call itself is slow we need to see token-level timings, otherwise the 'model' span just looks slow" — suggests later iteration to add nested subspan timings for tokenization vs decode.
- "On-call really wanted 'jump to first 5xx' button" — add as quick action on top bar.

Rough timeline for release: MVP (incident-mode + chips + heatline) in 2 sprints; follow-ups (collapse server-side + keyboard shortcuts + saved presets sync) in next 2 sprints.

Appendix: sample mock sequence (happy path)
1) On-call receives alert -> opens Console trace link -> small CTA "Enable incident view" -> toggles incident mode\2) Priority spans highlighted; user presses J to jump through p95 offenders -> lands on a span with retry-count 3 and status 502\3) User clicks "jump-to-parent" -> finds upstream proxy span with long DNS time -> pins that span and creates a ticket with pinned-context -> exports snapshot JSON and attaches to ticket.

End of doc.
